newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end sharply lower, led by gold.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end sharply lower, led by gold.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended sharply lower Monday, after a late sell-off, as the U.S. dollar and U.S. stocks and bonds recovered some ground.
But the sell-off was led by bullion dealers and many traders are convinced another European central bank sell program is underway.

"The gold market is deeply discouraged as it expected Friday's sell off in the stock market would result in a serious challenge to the $328.00 resistance level (basis spot gold), but it didn't happen," said Dinsa Mehta, Chase Manhattan's New York based managing director for global commodities.
"The market perceives there's some pretty heavyweight selling at that level and is gearing up for another sell off to a fresh test of the 12 year lows seen in July," he said.
COMEX December gold ended down $4.80 at $324.70 an ounce, after losing about $2.80 an ounce in the last half hour alone.
Estimated final COMEX gold volume was only moderate at 31,000 lots, but about 9,000 lots were traded in the last hour.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $321.10/60, compared to the London Monday afternoon fix at $322.60 and the New York close Friday around $325.80/30.

Implied gold lease rates edged higher again Monday to around 2.75 pct for one month, and 2.37 pct for 12 months, and are now back at their highest levels since January when the Dutch central bank announced a sale of 300 tonnes of gold.

The high and inverted gold forward lease rate curve reflected borrowing by bullion banks to finance a central bank forward sale program, as much as it did borrowing by funds or producers to finance fresh speculative short positions or hedge programs, bullion bank dealers and hedge fund sources said.

In fact in the CFTC Commitments of Traders report for the week ended August 12, released late Friday, net short positions held by funds fell sharply to 49,704 lots from 70,906 just a week earlier, suggesting much of the recovery in gold prices in recent weeks has been shortcovering by funds.

Meanwhile, some producer hedging has been noted by gold miners forced to enter into new hedges under certain bank financing arrangements, but most significant producer hedging was completed some weeks ago after spot gold prices slumped to 12 year lows around $315 an ounce, and some producers have been buying back hedges, analysts noted.

Australia's Sons of Gwalia Ltd announced Monday it had completed the restructuring of its hedge book, raising A$60 million, by closing out 295,000 ounces of put options and reducing the strike price on the remaining 2.39 million ounces of put options to an average of A$610 from A$638 an ounce.

The company said its hedge book now totalled 4.56 million ounces for delivery from 1997/98 through to 2006/2007 at an average price of A$629 per ounce. In Australia dollar terms, spot gold is currently trading around A$436.00 an ounce.
Last month Newmont Mining of the U.S. and South Africa's JCI Ltd announced hedge buy backs.

"The stockmarket stabilizing today gave funds another opportunity to sell short, and some companies have been entering into new forward sales, given their financing arrangements and the low gold price," said analyst Ted Kempf with New York based industry consultants, CPM Group.
"But central banks have also been pulling in gold for one reason or another pushing up lease rates," he said.

However, Dubai gold traders said Sunday they expected gold demand to rise in the next week after the Indian independence day holidays ended and ahead of the Indian harvest festival and wedding season in September.
COMEX September silver ended down 5.8 cents at $4.505 an ounce, giving back some of Friday's 15.5 cent gain which took the contract to its highest level since early July.
The CFTC Commitments of Traders report showed net short COMEX silver positions held by funds declined to 5,580 lots as of August 12 from 10,379 lots two weeks earlier.
NYMEX October platinum ended down $11.10 an ounce at $415.00, but NYMEX September palladium ended off just $1.80 at $203.00 and back months in NYMEX palladium ended higher.
Lease rates for platinum group metals (PGMs) were also lower Monday, with one month platinum falling to about 15 pct from 20 pct, and one month palladium easing to around 50 pct from 80 pct.
But the PGM forward curve remained heavily backwardated and metal remained in short supply, traders said.
